{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mi-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f8e8af47054f97988d7a662b8698412f97a3ef0b786f23ccefcf207716e726f7","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mi-class-std:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"7af7437894a2c63b20529c8a1ed7c10696796036051dd6666178ab579008ca37","source_liveness_sha256":"e81e5179580dc89fb25fdf5194e9f75291db3aa019fc21ccfe32c38d1a9df42f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Distracted driving, seat belts and child restraints","heading":"C — Distracted driving, seat belts and child restraints","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Distracted driving, seat belts and child restraints

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Federal highway safety officials estimate at least 3,400 deaths each year from crashes where a manual, visual or cognitive distraction pulled the driver's focus from controlling the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
That yearly death estimate may understate the problem, because it is hard to prove a distraction and its part in a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
A distracted driver who drives carelessly or negligently in a way likely to endanger people or property, or with willful or wanton disregard for their safety, can be prosecuted under Michigan law. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Holding a phone while driving is illegal in Michigan, which covers reading, texting, and making or answering a call, with exceptions for reporting crashes, crimes or other emergencies. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
The hand-held phone fine is $100 for a first offense and $250 for each later violation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
Anything that pulls your eyes from the road, your hands from the wheel or your mind from driving is a hazard, because the brain cannot fully attend to two activities at once. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
In the roughly quarter second the brain needs to switch between two tasks, a car going 65 mph travels 24 feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A01
Before driving, ask a front-seat passenger to handle maps or navigation, or plan your route in advance if you drive alone. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A01
Learn your vehicle's controls well enough to adjust temperature or radio settings without looking away from the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A02
Set radio presets and choose a playlist before you leave, and finish any grooming before starting out or after arriving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A02
Make sure children are comfortable and buckled before the trip, since tending to them while driving is a serious distraction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A02
While driving, avoid phones, texting devices and navigation or other electronic systems, and if you must call, park safely first. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A02
Do not take notes, read, look up numbers or get into stressful or confrontational conversations while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A02
If you eat while driving, pick easy-to-handle food and keep drinks secured in cup holders, and take a break if you feel tired or lost in thought. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A02
Michigan's general cell phone law, MCL 257.602b, bars every driver from holding or using a mobile electronic device such as a phone or tablet while operating a vehicle on a public road or other public venue. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A02
Banned uses include sending or receiving calls, sending, receiving or reading texts, viewing, recording or transmitting video, and reading or posting to social media. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A02
Any driver, including a teen, may use a device to text 9-1-1 or call police, a health-care provider, the fire department or another emergency service to report a medical emergency, crash, serious road hazard, fire or hazardous materials incident. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A02
The emergency exception also covers reporting a reckless or apparently impaired driver, or a crime in progress. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A02
Kelsey's Law, MCL 257.602c, bars teens holding a GDL Level 1 or Level 2 license from making or receiving non-emergency phone calls. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A02
GDL Level 3 teens and all other drivers may use GPS or navigation as long as they do not type information in by hand. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A02
Voice-operated or hands-free use is allowed if your hands stop after a single press, tap or swipe to start or end a function or pick a contact, or after using the vehicle's built-in interface. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A02
A dash cam that continuously records or broadcasts video, and a mounted device used in an already exempt way, are also allowed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A03
Under Click It or Ticket, an officer may stop a vehicle simply because the driver or passengers are not properly buckled. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A03
Michigan requires the driver and every front-seat passenger to wear a seat belt, and every passenger under 16 to be buckled in any seat. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A03
Children under 8, or shorter than 4 feet 9 inches, must ride in an approved car seat or booster seat in every seating position. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A03
Federal safety officials report seat belts save more than 13,000 lives a year, and buckling up is the most effective single step to protect yourself in a crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A03
Air bags do not replace a seat belt; wear the shoulder belt across the middle of the chest away from the neck and the lap belt low across the hips below the stomach. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A03
A driver excused from wearing a seat belt for a medical reason must carry a doctor's statement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A03
A child rides in a car seat or booster until reaching 8 years old or 4 feet 9 inches, whichever comes first, and parents are urged to go by height because a belt may not fit a small child. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A03
The child must be secured following the restraint and vehicle makers' instructions and federal safety standards. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A03
Taking a child out of a car seat to nurse while the vehicle is moving is prohibited. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A03
Children under 4 must ride in a rear seat when the vehicle has one, unless every rear seat is already filled by children under 4. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A03
A rear-facing child seat may go in the front only when the front passenger air bag is turned off. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A03
No one under 18 may ride in an open pickup bed above 15 mph, except for farm, construction, military, parade and authorized emergency or rescue uses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A03
Never hold a child on your lap or share one seat belt between a child and another passenger, and have children buckle up before you start the engine. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A03
Help installing a car seat is available from community agencies such as local health departments, and a certified technician can be found at cert.safekids.org under Find a Tech. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F37 | anchor: A03
Avoid secondhand car seats, which may not meet federal standards, may not work properly, or may be missing parts or instructions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]
